 UNC Bears football look to the future ahead of final home game of the season 
 UNC, 3-7, hosts nationally ranked No. 2 Montana State at noon Saturday at Nottingham Field

 University of Northern Colorado football quarterback Brayten Silbor (18) flexes in celebration as he helps direct the band in the fight song after UNC’s win over the Northeastern State RiverHawks in overtime during a college football game at Nottingham Field in Greeley on Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026. (Brice Tucker/Staff Photographer)
 By Anne Delaney | adelaney@greeleytribune.com | Greeley Tribune PUBLISHED: November 12, 2026 at 6:00 PM MST | UPDATED: November 14, 2026 at 3:56 PM MST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... The future is now for the University of Northern Colorado football team, Bears head coach Ed Lamb said this week.
 With a 3-7 overall record and 2-5 in the Big Sky Conference, the Bears can only look ahead. UNC has two games left in a long, up-and-down and at times frustrating season. Both of those games are against nationally ranked opponents, starting early Saturday afternoon.
 UNC hosts defending Big Sky champion and Football Championship Subdivision national champion Montana State at noon Saturday at Nottingham Field. The Bobcats (9-1, 6-1 Big Sky) come to Greeley ranked second in the two FCS polls — one from coaches and one from media. Montana State beat UNC 55-7 at Nottingham Field last year. 
 The following week, UNC has one final chance to win a road game when the Bears play Northern Arizona in Flagstaff, Arizona. UNC is 0-5 on the road this year. The Lumberjacks (8-2, 6-1) are ranked fifth in FCS polls this week. 
 Lamb said this year’s team is the best he’s had since he took over the program ahead of the 2023 season. The players and coaches are committed and capable, and the players can win on any given week, Lamb added.
 He has not led the players to enough wins, he said, and this is hard, painful and more frustrating. Lamb’s record is 8-37.
 “I’m proud of the team that we have. I’m not proud of our win-loss record,” Lamb said Monday. “Too many close ones. I may be a sure-fire Hall of Famer for the Hall of Fame of close losses in my career. It’s been painful at times in trying to turn this program around.”
 Northern Colorado Bears head coach Ed Lamb argues with a referee during a Big Sky Conference football game against the Cal Poly Mustangs at Nottingham Field in Greeley on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. (Brice Tucker/Staff Photographer) 
 Remember the Colorado State game last year in Fort Collins? Yes, that was a tough one.
 In the season opener at home way back on Aug. 28, UNC missed a game-tying extra point in the final three seconds against Big Sky opponent Weber State. 
 How might the Bears’ season be different now if they tied the Weber State game, got it to overtime and pulled out a win at home? To do that against a Big Sky rival … what would that have meant for the guys the rest of the year? 
 Two weeks later at Wyoming, UNC led 13-7 early in the fourth quarter and had the ball at the Cowboys’ 32-yard line following a lightning delay. 
 All the momentum was on the Bears’ sideline in Laramie. But a couple of penalties led to -5 yards on the drive, and UNC punted from inside Wyoming’s 40. 
 The Cowboys scored touchdowns on the next two drives and won 21-13. This was the second straight year UNC lost out on a chance to beat a bigger, Football Bowl Subdivision opponent. 
 Against Eastern Washington and against Southern Utah last week, UNC fell behind early. The Bears scratched and clawed their way back into both games but couldn’t finish off a comeback. 
 At Southern Utah last week, UNC trailed 24-7 at halftime. The Bears tied it with about two minutes left in the third quarter. Southern Utah regained the lead, 31-24 , on its next possession after a 15-play, nearly seven-minute drive. 
 UNC had two fourth-quarter drives after the Thunderbirds’ go-ahead TD. The Bears moved the ball to Southern Utah’s 19, but turned it over on downs after quarterback Brayten Silbor didn’t gain a yard on fourth and one on the first drive.
 On the second drive, UNC had first down at Southern Utah’s 26 with 18 seconds to play. A Southern Utah offsides penalty on third and 10 took UNC to third and five from the 21 with five seconds left.
 Northern Colorado Bears safety Franky Morales (6) tackles Weber State Wildcats quarterback Devin Brown (33) during the first ever night game at Nottingham Field on the campus of the University of Northern Colorado in Greeley on Friday, Aug. 28, 2026. (Brice Tucker/Staff Photographer) 
 UNC was called for a false start and was backed up to the 26. Silbor then threw an interception in the end zone on the final play.
 “We’re a great offense, a great team in general, but we’ve got to start faster because we put ourselves in holes that sometimes we can’t get out of,” Silbor said. “But that’s definitely one of the things we’re focusing on.”
 The Bears weren’t competitive in games against Montana and UC Davis.
 Lamb said when the team loses, it falls on the coaching staff. They’ve been out-coached and have to figure out how to improve. The UNC coaches won’t say the loss falls on the players.
Safety Franky Morales has a different take. He said a lot of the team’s losses come from a lack of execution by the players on critical plays and critical downs.
 “That’s really why we’ve fallen,” said Morales, a fifth-year player and a team captain. “So I think just us as players, it doesn’t come down to coaching for us to execute something. We have to lock in and execute in that moment. We have to live on in the moment and make the play, really.” 
 Senior Day
 Saturday’s game against Montana State is Senior Day, and UNC will honor 13 players who are ending their college careers:
 Defensive lineman Brennen Acosta from Lake Forest, California (El Toro High School, Saddleback College) 
 Running back Kieryus Boone from Saginaw, Michigan (Saginaw High School, Monterey Peninsula College) 
 Defensive lineman Ezra Ekuban from Parker (Regis Jesuit) 
 Wide receiver Dylan Evans from Little Elm, Texas (Little Elm High School, U.S. Air Force Academy) 
 Running back Justin Guin from Novato, California (San Marin High School, Fresno State) 
 Quarterback Kenny Lueth from Rocklin, California (Rocklin High School, American River College, Northern Illinois) 
 Defensive lineman Levi Little from Clovis, California (Buchanan High School, Fresno City College) 
 Defensive lineman Brooks Maile from Saint George, Utah (Pine View High School, Brigham Young University) 
 Defensive lineman Ayden Merrihew from Clovis, California (Clovis High School, Middle Tennessee State/Reedley College) 
 Safety Franky Morales from Chandler, Arizona (Chandler High School) 
 Quarterback Keegan Patterson from Longmont (Longmont High School, University of Southern California, Northwest Mississippi Community College/Indiana State)
 Quarterback Brayten Silbor from Scottsdale, Arizona (Chaparral High School, Lehigh/Southwestern College) 
 Safety Alfred Smith from Phoenix, Arizona (Chandler High School School) 
 How to watch or listen
 Tickets for the game at Nottingham Field are available at tickets.unco.edu .
 Television broadcast coverage: ESPN+/Scripps Sports.
 Radio: Pirate Radio at 93.5 FM, pirateradio935.com .
